title: Intraspinal injection of adeno-associated viruses into the adult mouse spinal cord
protocol: Transfer the mouse to the surgical area.
Place the mouse on the window of the metal plate such that the underside of the mouse is exposed to the heating pad.
Tape the forelimbs to the metal plate.
Insert a 3 mL syringe or similarly sized wedge under the lower neck/upper back of the mouse.
Tape the hindlegs and the tail at two points.
Ensure the mouse remains taut along the rostro-caudal axis throughout the procedure.
Apply eye lubricant on both eyes of the mouse to prevent drying during surgery.
Sterilize the surgical site by swabbing the skin with three alternating rubs of povidone-iodine and 70% ethanol.
Make a 2 cm long incision starting at the base of the head and extending through the midline of the back using a scalpel.
Slide blunt forceps under the rostral margin of the incision.
Use a retractor at the mouse’s head to retract the skin.
Retract the skin along the caudal margin on either side with other retractors to create a triangular surgical window.
Locate the margin between the trapezius muscle and the adipose tissue in the exposed tissue.
Gently cut any fascia holding the two pieces of tissue along this margin using micro scissors.
Adjust the rostrally placed retractor to tuck away the musculature.
Adjust other retractors to tuck away the adipose tissue.
Locate the prominent, long spinous process of the second thoracic vertebra (T2 vertebra).
Snip the muscles attached rostrally to the T2 vertebra using micro scissors.
Slide micro scissors underneath the rostrally located musculature and cut along the midline to detach it from underlying cervical vertebrae.
Use two retractors, one on either side of the mouse, to retract midline muscles.
Count up from T2 to locate appropriate cervical segments for injection.
Gently swab exposed vertebrae with an absorption triangle to remove residual tissue.
Puncture meninges using a fine-tipped forceps to facilitate micropipette entry into spinal cord.
Peel away meninges to obtain clear view of spinal cord segments.
Using a scalpel, make an incision 2 cm in length starting ∼1 cm rostral to the middle of the hump.
Gently cut the musculature along the midline of the hump with micro scissors to expose the underlying vertebrae.
Locate the T12-T13 vertebral junction at the peak of the hump.
Identify lumbar segments by counting up or down from the identified vertebra.
Palpate the 13th rib and trace its point of insertion into the spinal cord to locate the T13 vertebra.
Expose the 13th rib by pulling down the incised skin along the left margin.
Use magnetic retractors if necessary to increase the area exposed under the skin.
Cut away the tissue holding the vertebrae together to reveal the underlying spinal segments.
Soak excess blood using absorption triangles during lumbar surgeries.
Gently swab the exposed vertebrae with absorption triangles to remove any residual tissue and obtain a clear view of the spinal segments.
Carefully puncture the meninges and peel it away to facilitate smooth entry of the micropipette into the spinal cord.
Transfer the mouse along with the metal plate to the stereotaxic stage after exposing relevant spinal cord segments.

Adjust the metal plate containing the mouse and the arms of the stereotaxic manipulator such that the micropipette tip is positioned directly above the surface of the first spinal segment to be injected.
Ensure the micropipette is 400-600 μm away from the midline.
Set the total volume and rate of release on the syringe pump for viral particle injections.
Gently lower the micropipette using axis manipulators on the stereotaxic injector until it just touches the spinal cord surface.
Tare the dorso-ventral coordinate reading to ensure accurate depth measurement during injections.
Gently lower the micropipette to a depth of 500 μm and pull back 200 μm for dorsal laminae infection, so that the micropipette tip settles at ∼300 μm from the dorsal surface.
Gently lower the micropipette to a depth of 800-1000 μm and withdraw 200 μm for ventral laminae infection, so that the micropipette tip settles at a depth of ∼600–800 μm from the dorsal surface.
Wait one minute after injection before pulling the micropipette out to ensure efficient tissue absorption.
Run the program until a small drop of viral solution is seen pooling at the tip before proceeding to inject the next segment.
Move the metal plate containing the mouse to a flat surface.
Wait for bleeding, if any, to stop.
Gently remove the retractors holding the muscles.
Suture the midline muscles using a 6-0 absorbable suture.
Remove the retractors holding the skin.
Close the skin wound with wound clips or 6-0 sutures.
Reverse the anesthesia by intraperitoneally injecting an appropriate volume of the reversal drug cocktail.
Return the mouse to its home cage.
Place a hot pack or hand warmer on the cage floor overnight to counteract any loss in body temperature.
Ensure that the ambient temperature in the incubator is around 25°C–27°C if using an incubator for post-operative care.
Remove the top lid or air filter of the cage placed in the incubator to ensure adequate ventilation.
Place a few food pellets on the floor of the cage for a day.
Administer analgesics using a 1mL syringe with a 26-gauge needle.
Gently place the mouse on the steel food rack to lift it away from the rack floor by lifting the tail.
Swiftly inject the mouse in the intraperitoneal space.
Monitor mice for signs of spinal damage the day after surgery.
Euthanize mice displaying paralysis.
